title: Officer said he thought he was being threatened: Inquest hears how Keldon McMillan died
article: A city police officer who fired the shotgun blast that ended a pistol-wielding man's life thought his life was in danger, he testified Tuesday at an inquest into the man's death.
Const. Gary David said he had been on the scene in a darkened field less than a minute when Keldon McMillan spun around and fired twice in his direction.
David said he only saw muzzle flashes.
"I was faced with the threat of being shot," he testified.
A police dog who was running to attack McMillan took the bullets instead. David said he did not know the dog had been hit until later.
David and two other officers then opened fire, but only his shots struck McMillan.
The wounded man, even as he lay face down on the ground with eight shotgun pellets in his body, then raised his gun as though taking aim once again, David testified.
Another officer jumped on McMillan's hand and pinned it to the ground until he was handcuffed.
David, a 13-year veteran who teaches an officer safety course about high-risk situations, told the inquest police officers at the scene acted in perfect accordance with their training.
They gave McMillan every possible opportunity to end the situation without violence, even though he'd already fired his gun into the air once, he said.
McMillan, a 33-year-old home builder, died May 21, 2001, after leading city police and the RCMP on a high-speed chase from his home in northeast Saskatoon.

Witnesses, including his wife, have testified that he was depressed over marital and financial problems, had repeatedly threatened suicide in the three weeks before his death and had said there would be a shootout if police were called.
Dr. Rani Kanthan, the pathologist who conducted McMillan's autopsy, testified his blood alcohol level was approaching twice the legal limit for driving at the time of his death.

Traces of anabolic steroids and cocaine were also found in his body, but Kanthan was unable to determine when McMillan may have taken them. The cocaine could have been taken any time in the previous 10 days, she said.
Several of McMillan's relatives attending the inquest declined comment, although family members have said in the past police could have saved McMillan's life by backing off and giving him some space.
But David said that was simply not in the cards with an armed suspect and a farmhouse nearby.
"For us to let him leave that area with a weapon was not appropriate."
